; Bank three veneers expose player update, primary/secondary projectile update, actor callbacks and sprite drawing. Effective PRG context is [6,7,14,15]. Additional slots enter credits setup and recovery-choice services.
; Jump to the ending text/credits sequence at $b32d. Its self-initializing caller in the fixed bank was exercised artificially.

; Jump to the classified bank-local service at $b754. Its complete event meaning is described at that routine, not inferred from the veneer alone.
; Enter the terrain-position reset helper.

; Clear the per-frame player event byte, latch controller input unless inhibited and prioritize terrain/contact transitions. Then update animation, damage sequences, movement, camera mode and boundary handling. Overlay/scripted modes suppress ordinary movement.
; Event byte $0313 equal to $c2 sets $f3=$ff before the event byte is cleared. The original event name remains unresolved.

; Clear event/scratch, then choose scripted contact motion, scene transition or ordinary input handling. PlayerUpdateInhibit substitutes zero input; otherwise copy ControllerActions into player-local $10.
; Clear player-local input $10 before shared movement processing. This is reached under PlayerUpdateInhibit.
; Copy current controller actions into player-local scratch $10.

; Cancel movement for active metatile patches, process terrain/damage state and stop on the transition flag $f5. Otherwise update animation, bounds, controls and camera; state/damage flags can skip individual systems.
; Choose zero for the shared player contact-state update.

; Update horizontal and vertical motion, screen bounds, camera selection, acceleration/reversal and terrain transitions, then finalize velocities. Player mode bit $10 applies an additional scene-bound camera constraint.
; Run the shared velocity cleanup before returning from the player update; branches throughout the update converge here.
; Any high-nibble patch request clears player camera-follow flag $40, camera velocity and CameraMotionMode. This prevents ordinary scrolling during overlay changes.

; Ignore a negative boundary/state byte. A hard terrain contact enters one of two damage sequences; other contacts update the standing/falling flag and invoke forced motion when required. Zero input is forced during hard contacts. Exact damage-type names are unresolved, so the two sequences are named by their contact source.

; On first entry set sound selector one, install animation pointer $aa0d and state one, then decode its header. Later frames tick animation every four counts; negative phase counts down the recovery delay before scene reset.
; Choose zero and join the shared damage-animation continuation.
; At phase count $20 reset the counter and mark the damage state negative.
; Count down the remaining recovery delay. On underflow decrement the transition latch and reset the scene; otherwise request player state $40 and initialize recovery animation.

; Parallel damage path uses sound selector two, animation pointer $aa29 and state two. Advance animation every four counts; animation flag bit two marks the recovery phase negative. Count down recovery, clear transient player state, then run the shared recovery delay and scene-reset path.
; Choose zero for the shared hard-contact animation continuation.
; Animation motion flag bit two ends this phase by marking the damage state negative; otherwise retain its phase.
; Mirror the recovery countdown: underflow enters scene reset; otherwise install player state $40 and recovery animation.

; Store incoming A into player movement, contact, damage, local-input and camera-mode fields. Recovered callers pass zero; the helper itself does not force zero. It does not reset persistent scene/equipment state.

; Clear camera coordinates, saved offsets and mode; restore bank service state. Serialize CHR value $15 under the mapper guard, set transition selection, draw its screen and mark transition active. The trailing entry initializes recovery time and player Y/X to $50.

; Install default animation pointers/timing constants, clear scroll/input/projectile counts and derive equipment-dependent player fields. Reset the two three-slot projectile state arrays while retaining their low-nibble type selectors.
; Four finite transition choices used by the direction/animation consumer.

; If player boundary flags $e0 are set, clear camera-follow bit $40. Depending on boundary side, keep camera motion only while the corresponding right/left input is held; otherwise zero CameraMotionMode.

; Hard contact bypasses this work. Player resource byte $03bb at one marks a state bit; zero/negative sets player mode bit seven and invokes forced movement. On ordinary frames compare scene-parity-dependent bottom bounds and contact flags before marking hard contact. Resource/death interpretation is tentative; mechanics are explicit.

; Directional input selects fixed or equipment-table vertical velocity, counts a sixteen-frame facing toggle and updates fractional Y through the shared integrator. Ground/boundary flags can mark hard contact. This is a forced-motion state, not an assumed normal flight path.

; Inspect player boundary flags, terrain state, scene menu and ScrollVariant. A pending bit-$20 condition becomes an inhibited scroll transition, setting player state bit seven, flag $0304 bit zero and clearing uploads. Later animation/scroll gates clear those bits.

; If entry bit $20 is clear, position player at X=$28/Y=$bb, reset motion/animation and set the entry bit. Unless camera Y page two or inhibit mode two, integrate Y velocity $ff00 upward, update scroll-transition flags and eventually clear contact bit two.

; Skip scripted negative state, equipment scene or unrelated variants. Scroll variants three/four set movement gate $0304 bit zero; scene and camera-page checks advance animation at the transition boundary and clear the gate once ordinary updates can resume.

; When uninhibited, run every eight ticks. Select animation transitions from scene position, boundary flags, local Start latch, facing and horizontal input. Transition selection follows pointer entries in the current descriptor.
; Use descriptor offset eight before joining the shared animation selector.
; Use offset Y into the current animation descriptor pointer (stored low at $02f0, high at $02ef) to load a new descriptor, then decode its six-byte header. The caller selects the transition offset.

; Combine movement mode, boundary/contact flags, facing and horizontal input to select screen motion or camera-follow motion. Active reversal/transition state gates changes; the special-facing path latches boundary bit six when X reaches $80.
; Choose zero for the shared horizontal-transition path.
; Unless boundary bit zero blocks movement, initialize horizontal velocity/animation, set the motion gate and update the camera-follow calculation.
; Call the left-input latch helper, then use carry and boundary bits to choose the velocity/camera update. The special facing path has its own initialization and latch.

; On carry set run the special facing transition; otherwise clear the facing latch and accept left input. Boundary bit one suppresses the velocity change; accepted input clears the motion gate and updates camera motion.

; Before camera-follow mode, load the player speed, apply horizontal movement and set camera-follow bit $40 after reaching X=$80. In follow mode, boundary flags may suppress motion; otherwise select alternate speed, negate it as required by the shared facing transform and integrate X.
; First initialize motion and wait for X to reach $80, then latch boundary bit six. Subsequent frames choose direction two and update velocity unless blocked by boundary bit one.

; Skip negative player mode and active vertical acceleration. Load equipment-dependent vertical speed; down/up input latches and boundary flags choose direction. One path negates the signed 16-bit velocity, clears top/bottom boundary flags and integrates Y.

; Only player boundary flag bit zero enables this path. Ignore negative vertical state and mode bit zero; check top/bottom bounds and input. Otherwise clear the vertical bounds, set fractional downward step $40 and integrate a slow Y drift.
; Carry set joins the established vertical-motion continuation.

; Only nonnegative player mode with suitable contact flags/terrain permits sliding. Count down a six-frame phase, set mode bit zero, derive and negate equipment vertical speed, and combine horizontal/vertical integration according to input/scroll state. At completion clear the mode and velocity state.
; Set player terrain-contact bit zero before applying horizontal motion, with a flag-dependent direction adjustment through the shared negation helper.
; If player flag $0304 bit two is set, negate horizontal velocity, then fall through to the X integrator.
; Add fractional X velocity $02ee into fraction $02ec, then signed whole-pixel velocity $02ed and carry into PlayerScreenX. Byte arithmetic supplies wrap behavior.
; Unless mode bit zero is active, set vertical motion request $030b to one, then enter the Y integrator.
; Add fractional Y velocity $02ea into fraction $02e8, then signed whole-pixel velocity $02e9 and carry into PlayerScreenY.
; Add fractional step $030d to Y fraction, carrying only into screen Y. This path supplies no signed whole-pixel step.
; Player speed selector $0316 indexes little-endian fractional/whole X velocity pairs at $890c.
; Use the alternate little-endian speed table at $8914 with the same selector.
; Negate the 16-bit fractional/whole X velocity using scratch $b4/$b3.
; Negate the 16-bit fractional/whole Y velocity using scratch $b4/$b3.
; Eight two-byte fractional/whole camera speed pairs selected by equipment and facing; consumer chooses the relevant half.
; Subtract the signed whole/fraction velocity from the camera fractional pair and return.

; Set left/right flags at X below $1f or at least $e1; clear them inside. Set top flag below Y=$20. Scene parity selects bottom Y=$b7/$c7; even scenes clamp to $b7 and zero Y fraction. Clear top/bottom flags when inside.

; Reject camera updates during overlay/scripted/acceleration states. Right/left inputs and boundary/facing flags choose CameraMotionMode one/two; terrain-contact bit three inhibits selected motion. Direction latches retain the previous accepted input during acceleration.
; A clear carry skips direction changes; otherwise clear the direction scratch and join the common exit.

; Clamp screen position, then reconcile ScrollVariant, boundary flags, input latches and acceleration state. Choose screen-space acceleration or camera acceleration, retain a latched direction while moving and stop/reset the phase at blocked contacts or completed steps. Scene-eight camera Y page zero adds a special boundary gate.

; For eligible player modes away from boundaries, mark acceleration state $40, load a velocity from the four-step $8c2a table, integrate X and increment the phase every four ticks. A special mode left-edge case clears acceleration.

; Reject overlay changes and blocked player modes. With scrolling active, mark acceleration state $80 and every four ticks load the next camera fractional/whole step from $8c32, incrementing the phase. With scrolling inactive, clear acceleration/contact state as appropriate.

; Require an active vertical-motion request and no top/bottom or forced-slide state. Latch direction, load a four-step velocity from $8c2a, negate for the selected up direction and integrate Y. Advance phase every seven ticks; boundary contact or phase four clears all vertical acceleration/latch fields.
; Two-byte movement values read by the vertical integration setup; selector meaning is partly equipment-dependent.

; Under active resource/ordinary player state with no Select, scrolling or acceleration, test top/bottom boundary flags and adjacent terrain. Empty terrain at that boundary selects inhibit mode two/one and clears pending uploads. Exact scene transition meaning remains tentative.

; Apply a scene-eleven corner rule, then clamp to X=$20 or $e0 according to facing when outside its allowed edge. Clear fractional/whole X motion, terrain horizontal-contact bit and acceleration state after a clamp.
; At the caller scene-eleven camera corner, boundary byte exactly five clears horizontal acceleration and terrain contact bit zero.

; Clear horizontal velocity when boundary/contact state requires. Unless forced-slide/vertical request/input needs it, also clear Y velocity. This preserves active motion while preventing stale velocity on idle frames.
; When no overlay patch or horizontal acceleration is active, load camera fractional/whole speed from equipment-selected pairs at $8d60.
; Input-latch masks; accepted nonzero bits keep the complementary pop path from executing.

; Test local input bit one. On a press record it in horizontal direction $02f8 and, when horizontal acceleration is idle, in its initial direction $030c. Return carry set for accepted held input, clear for absence.
; Mirror the right-input latch using bit two and the same horizontal direction/initial-direction fields. Return presence in carry.
; Test local input bit four and update vertical direction $02fa; when vertical acceleration is idle also update initial direction $0310. Return presence in carry.
; Mirror the down-input latch using bit eight and the same vertical direction fields. Return presence in carry.
; GameplayFrameCounter bit one alternates between the two sprite-definition pointers in the current animation header. Return selected pointer in $37/$38.
; Count $02f9 toward $28. Before that point move screen X right by one pixel and select the sprite definition; at completion clear terrain contacts and the counter.

; At scene nine and the required camera cell, accept the scripted input transition. Otherwise move Y toward $72, then X toward $20, and clear the alignment request. The second entry latches/releases right input at the specified camera boundary.
; At camera X page one, right input or a negative horizontal acceleration state clears player camera-follow bit $40 and CameraMotionMode. Other positions leave it unchanged.

; At scene three, camera Y page three/X page ten/fine X at least $b8, set scripted player mode bit three and advance its positioning sequence. Once mode bit two is reached, mark overlay descriptor $02cd active and request patch $c7.

; While no negative patch request is pending, stop camera motion, select sprite definition and increase camera fine X toward $ff. Move player screen X toward $40; once positioned set mode bit two, clear mode bit three, initialize the script buffer and clear horizontal acceleration.
; Copy 29 fixed bytes from $8f64 to RAM $0220. The full higher-level animation/effect schema remains unresolved.
; Bounded terrain-response bytes; nearby consumer and neighbors delimit the non-code span. Full event meanings remain unresolved.

; Read six bytes from the current descriptor: flags/facing state, shared motion/shape flags and two sprite-definition pointers. Store them in persistent player state; transition links beyond the header are selected by FollowPlayerAnimationLink.

; Skip the terminal negative damage phase. Read shape and three alternative part counts from the selected definition, choosing count by player flags/mode. Each four-byte part adds Y/X offsets to player screen position, copies tile/attributes and appends to OAM. This format uses byte addition without the actor helper clipping.

; Disable rendering, wait for vblank, write the choice-screen tile streams and restore PPU shadows. A separate input entry toggles the two choices and accepts Start into a four-tick recovery delay. Tile streams terminate at $ff.
; Four $ff-terminated tile streams for the recovery choice screen; individual starts are $9102/$910d/$9116/$911c.
; Select animation descriptor offset six, then reuse the terrain/input reset helper.

; Count four or more enters pool reset. Zero count deactivates three slots, then dispatch by primary type through its five-pointer table. Handlers scan free slots, accept fire, initialize individual/group projectiles, integrate motion, apply bounds and advance impact animation.
; Clear per-slot impact state and active high bits across three slots, then enter type dispatch.

; Scan slots two down to zero, storing the last slot index in $0347. Free slots test the fire latch; accepted slots set active bit seven, increment count and initialize origin/velocity. Active projectiles then run motion, bounds and hit-state passes.

; Scan three slots for accepted fire input and initialize newly active projectiles. Alternate type setup may activate the whole pool after eligibility tests. Run movement, bounds and impact updates only while the active count is nonzero; carry helpers report whether a negative active slot exists.

; Reject firing while player is inhibited, damaged or hard-contacted. Local controller bit $40 is edge-latched in $0354. A new press queues event sound three unless a higher-priority sound gate prevents replacement, and returns carry set.

; Reject inhibited or damaged player modes. Debounce fire every eight ticks, honor controller bit six, and queue sound selector three only when lower-priority sound permits. Carry reports accepted input.

; Facing and player motion/animation flags select an origin/velocity direction index. Type one uses a distinct origin offset table; other types use the ordinary table. Resolve type animation pointers and direction-based signed fractional/whole X/Y velocities into the selected projectile slot.

; Facing and equipment select three direction bytes, origin offsets, animation pointers and signed X/Y velocity pairs. Store each member in the three-slot parallel arrays; helper entries load directions and initial coordinates.
; For slots down from $0347, skip inactive or hit-marked projectiles. Integrate fractional X/Y velocities into byte positions and cache the resulting positions for bounds checks.

; Test active projectile cached positions against facing-dependent X edge, player motion and scene-parity Y bounds. Some bottom contacts enter hit animation; others clear active state to the low type nibble and decrement count. Scene eight camera-page zero has a special bottom rule.

; For hit-marked slots, queue sound four once and follow animation transition link eight. Decode sprite pointers, advance hit phase and after six steps clear hit state, deactivate the projectile and decrement count. Other slots retain their current state.

; When projectiles are active and player updates uninhibited, scan active slots, read sprite flags/count from each animation pointer and append count four-byte offset parts to OAM around the projectile Y/X. A per-slot scratch index survives the shared OAM helper.

; Packed coordinate offsets, direction values and definition references. Consumers select paired origin coordinates and four-byte sprite/state headers; exact larger layout is not inferred from rebuilding.
; Five little-endian code pointers. Type-specific pool/fire/state contracts support the handler bodies; natural selection of every type is separate.
; Little-endian CPU entry words in this span's effective PRG context.
; Direction triples, definition references and facing-selected group initializers. Separate origins $9635/$963b select the three-slot direction records.

; Counts four or more enter cleanup; zero count clears active bits in three slots. Type dispatch has sixteen supported pointer entries. Recovered handlers choose one/two slots and their initialization, target tracking, movement and impact paths.
; Advance the secondary slot reset loop, then enter type dispatch.
; Select slot zero as the last processed index and begin the ordinary secondary projectile scan.
; Select slot one as the last processed index, so the scan visits one then zero.
; Select slot zero and enter the shared ordinary secondary scan.
; Select slot zero and enter the single-slot special-type path at $9764.
; Alternate type entries select slot zero or one and set the spawn cursor before joining the shared updater.

; A free slot tests the secondary fire latch, sets active bit seven, increments count and selects normal versus type-five/six initialization. After scanning, choose type-specific velocity, bounds and impact updates. The last index $0398 defines the independently bounded slot passes.
; Load ordinary secondary velocity, integrate position, apply screen bounds and advance the ordinary impact animation.
; Load the alternate velocity phase, then use ordinary movement, bounds and impact updates.
; Use alternate velocity/movement with the long-lived impact state and camera-relative boundary behavior.

; If slot zero is inactive, test the fire latch and activate/initialize it on acceptance. Active slots run velocity/target phases, signed integration, bounds, impact animation and reservation cleanup.
; Accepted fire sets the active bit, increments the pool count and initializes slot zero.

; Run per-slot targeting, movement, boundary, hit-animation and reservation cleanup. Each inactive slot has a separate accepted-fire initialization path; X/Y slot fields remain separate parallel arrays.

; Reject firing during player inhibition, hard terrain contact or damage state. Edge-latch local controller bit $80 in $0355. Accepted requests choose sound five or seven for types five/six, respecting the existing event-sound priority gate, and return carry set.

; Facing/type choose an origin direction and a projectile-definition pointer. Type two has fixed direction indices three/four; others combine facing and player animation flags. Place projectile at player position plus direction offsets, load four animation/state pointer bytes and save the direction selector per slot.

; Facing selects origin direction three/four. Type five uses facing-dependent definitions; type six uses the shared third definition. Place the projectile, then load the same four pointer bytes as the ordinary initializer.
; Read four bytes from the selected definition into the current slot sprite/state pointer arrays. This shared interior entry is also reached when advancing a state link.
; Mirrored entries initialize slot zero/one from facing, direction and definition pointers. Resolve origin offsets against player X/Y and copy the two sprite/state pointer pairs.
; For active slots, use a fixed initial direction for twelve counts, then use the saved per-slot direction to choose signed fractional/whole X/Y velocities from parallel tables.

; While A remains held, use a dedicated vertical velocity and zero X velocity. On release choose a facing-dependent motion pair, then set player shared-projectile flag bit one. This controls the single-slot type-two path.

; For the first two counts load a direction-selected horizontal velocity and zero Y. Afterwards optionally follow an animation state link (except type six) and add downward acceleration $0060 to Y velocity each tick.
; For active slots, apply the camera fractional/whole displacement, negating the pair for reverse scrolling.

; For active slot zero with a nonnegative phase byte, increment its phase, derive facing direction and load the phase velocity. At phase four replace the counter with $80, ending further phase stepping.

; Advance slot-one startup phase. Targeting entries for both slots periodically retain or acquire an eligible main/small actor, excluding actor kind $26; per-actor reservation bits distinguish the two projectile slots. Compute a direction toward its signed fractional coordinates and reload sprite and velocity pointers.
; Scan slots from $0398 down to zero, skipping inactive or impact-marked slots. Integrate fractional/whole X and Y velocities into positions using per-slot fraction accumulators.
; For each active slot without a negative impact state, add signed whole/fraction velocities to X and Y with carry propagation.
; Direction $038c selects parallel fractional/whole X/Y velocity pairs at $b21d/$b2c7 for slot zero.
; Use its direction index to load signed whole/fraction X/Y velocity pairs from the two tables.

; Skip inactive and already impact-marked slots. Facing selects X edge six/$f4, scene parity selects bottom Y=$bc/$dc and top is nine. Some ground contacts set impact bit seven; others call the shared retirement helper. Scene eight at camera Y page zero retires at the bottom directly.

; First apply ordinary bounds. Impact flag $40 permits camera-relative X compensation when scrolling; flag $10 suppresses further adjustment. Add/subtract camera step by ScrollVariant and retire at the corresponding edge $f8/eight.

; Compare each active projectile against facing-dependent X and scene-dependent Y bounds. Mark impact where appropriate, or clear tracking/active state and decrement the count when the slot leaves its domain.

; For the selected last slot, follow pointer link at offset four in its animation/state descriptor, then reuse the four-byte pointer loader. This is an interior transition helper with X chosen from $0398.

; For hit-marked slots queue sound six once, follow impact link eight and set flag $20. Repeatedly advance the two-branch animation helper; retire after sixteen impact ticks. Other active slots retain their current state.

; Hit-marked projectiles with flag $40 are pinned to Y=$c0 and count sixty ticks before setting flag $10. Then queue impact sound/link once and run the same sixteen-tick impact animation before retirement. Distinct flags separate grounded duration from the terminal impact phase.

; On first impact queue sound six and follow the definition link at offset eight. Advance each impact animation, then after sixteen ticks clear its active, tracking, phase and target fields and decrement the pool count.

; A per-slot phase byte alternates descriptor links at offsets two/four every two ticks, reloads the sprite pointer and increments the phase. Independently compensate X for active scrolling by adding/subtracting camera velocity so the effect stays tied to world position.
; Mirrored slot entries alternate links at offsets two/four every two counts, load the sprite pointer and compensate camera X displacement while the impact remains active.

; Clear secondary phase/impact/linkage counters, retain low-nibble type bits in state/flags, clear the player shared-projectile bit and decrement SecondaryProjectileCount. Callers must supply an active slot to avoid count underflow.
; When a projectile slot is inactive, clear its $80/$40 reservation bit across the four reservation entries.

; Skip drawing with zero count or player inhibition. Scan active slots, read animation flags/count and append each four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X offset record around projectile position. Save slot index separately while the shared OAM helper runs.
; Seventeen coordinate pairs selected by projectile direction; first coordinate is X offset and second Y offset in the initializer.

; Sixteen little-endian code pointers interleaved with definition-pointer origins used by the initializers; consumer-specific entry origins are retained. No uniform word interpretation is imposed on unrelated subfields.
; Little-endian CPU entry words in this span's effective PRG context.
; Subtract fractional/whole Y and X positions. Their signs form exactly selector zero/two/four/six, choosing one of four compatible direction bodies with a shared RTS continuation.
; Four little-endian code pointers indexed by zero/two/four/six, independently bounded by the first quadrant body.
; Little-endian CPU entry words in this span's effective PRG context.

; Four mirrored quadrant bodies compare high nibbles of absolute X/Y distances and their difference to select an axial or diagonal direction. The turn helper maps directions to a sixteen-position ring and advances one step along the shorter arc.
; Seventeen direction-to-ring cells followed by sixteen ring-to-direction cells and boundary data. Turning uses modulo sixteen; exact direction game names remain mechanical.

; Advance the player-linked reach animation, then check its proximity/contact state against actor slot seven. Probably rescue-related, given its actor/player alignment and capture flags; exact event meaning is not established by these mechanics alone.

; Hard contact cancels the active reach flag; player mode bit six also clears its high state. Actor slot seven must be active, below the player by less than $50 and within $60 horizontally to begin tracking. Otherwise an already-active animation retracts. The low selector chooses one of two reach-length/animation chains.

; Choose one of two fixed descriptor chains ($b0fb/$b133), set a six-tick step delay, mark state active and load its first sprite pointer plus forward link. The low reach selector distinguishes the two chains.
; Every six ticks quantize vertical separation to actor slot seven, compare with the currently displayed reach step $03b2 and follow the forward/backward descriptor link until matched.
; Same six-tick reach tracking, but enter the distance quantizer at its second threshold group. This changes the mapping from vertical separation to selected frame.
; From current reach descriptor, load the sprite pointer and the forward descriptor link at offsets two/three.
; Load the sprite pointer and backward descriptor link at offsets four/five. The descriptor therefore begins with sprite pointer, forward link and backward link.
; Convert separation A into step one through six using thresholds four/$0c/$14/$1c/$24. Return step in $86. Interior entry $a7f1 starts at the $14 threshold for the longer reach mode.
; Every eight ticks follow the backward link until descriptor pointer reaches $b0f3; then clear active state to its low selector nibble and reset the displayed-step byte.
; Use the same eight-tick backward-link sequence, stopping at descriptor $b12b before clearing active/displayed state.
; Only active reach state with no hard player contact draws. Resolve sprite pointer and part count, add player Y/X to each four-byte part, then emit through the shared OAM service.
; Read the remaining tile/attribute/X fields, add player X, emit the four-byte part through the shared OAM service and repeat for the remaining count.

; With nonzero excluded/proximity actor count, test direct player alignment first. Active reach state can also set actor slot seven pending flag $40 when vertical separation is below $3c or $2c (by reach selector) and horizontal distance is under three. Actor field $045b=$ff suppresses this reach contact.

; If actor slot seven is within six pixels horizontally and less than eight pixels below the player, set its pending flag $80. Comparisons retain the original unsigned vertical subtraction. This establishes alignment mechanics without proving a completed rescue encounter.

; Composite sprite/animation records: pointer-like prefix and repeated coordinate, tile and attribute fields. Nearby actor consumers were inspected; individual record boundaries and game roles remain unresolved.

; Enable the queued single-tile writer and initialize video/ending state. Reveal one token every six NMI signals. After eight lines and a finite delay, initialize credits; update credit motion and OAM until its completion predicate. Artificial execution reached the message and credits; natural completion remains separate.
; The first byte returns from the preceding routine. The following entry clears credit objects and initializes their first record group.
; Update credit-entry motion, build OAM, consume NMI and test the final-entry predicate. Carry set exits after the finite final delay.
; Consume FrameReady exactly like the main-loop handshake; this bank-local helper does not count every NMI that may have occurred before entry.
; Initialize queued PPU write address $20e2, clear request/color/text line/column counters and set a $40 post-text delay. The NMI single-tile writer later consumes $fa/$fb/$fc/$fd.

; For line indices below eight, resolve its text pointer and read the next token. $ff advances the line/address; ordinary glyphs advance the queued PPU address, optionally queue sound three except glyph $f0, then mark one pending tile write.
; Increment the line index, add $40 to the queued PPU address and reset the token cursor before resuming the ending loop.
; Line counter eight decrements the $40 delay and returns carry set when finished. Earlier line counts return carry clear.
; Set carry and join the shared completion return.
; Line pointer prefix followed by tile tokens. Ending consumer bounds its eight lines and uses $ff line terminators; complementary branches exclude instruction fallthrough into the table.

; Wait until prior OAM DMA is consumed, reset sprite allocation, set drawing scratch and build all credit records. Hide unused OAM slots and queue DMA. Adjacent interior helper expands each record as a horizontal tile run.

; Counter $0220 supplies the number of credit records. Each state low six bits selects a tile-string pointer at $b639; first byte counts tiles. Emit one sprite per tile at record Y and X plus eight times tile index, attributes zero. Advance to the next record until the count is consumed.

; Clear actor/credit parallel fields and counters. The next entry selects the next group pointer, copies count and state/target pairs, places each object at Y $fe/X $10 and advances the finite group index. Group index seven waits in place.
; Little-endian group pointers and count-prefixed state/target pairs. The credit loader initializes each object's Y/X separately and advances a finite group index.

; Scan negative/active credit states and move entries with flag $40 toward their stored target Y using per-entry step $03ec. An entry passing Y=$e0 sets flag $40 on the next record, chaining credit motion. The completion helper separately checks the last record target.
; Compare the last credit record Y with its target field. Mismatch returns carry clear; matching entries count the final delay to $f0, reset it and return carry set.
; Increment the final delay and continue its predicate until reaching $f0.

; Bounded initializer table and lookup records; exact game-level names remain unresolved.
